plain.text: King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church, intending to persecute them. He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword. Seeing that this pleased the Jewish leaders, he arrested Peter too, during the Passover festival, planning to put him on trial publicly afterwards.

Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him. The night before his trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains. Suddenly an angel appeared and a light shone in the cell. The angel struck Peter on the side and woke him: "Quick, get up!" The chains fell off. Peter followed, thinking he was seeing a vision. They passed the guards and the iron gate opened by itself. Then the angel left him. Peter realised, "Now I know without a doubt that the Lord rescued me." He went to the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, where many had gathered to pray. A servant girl named Rhoda recognised his voice, and in her joy ran back without opening the door! They said, "You're out of your mind," but Peter kept knocking. When they opened, they were astonished. He told them how the Lord had brought him out, and then went elsewhere. In the morning Herod could not find him and had the guards executed.

Later, Herod gave a speech to the people of Tyre and Sidon, wearing his royal robes. They shouted, "This is the voice of a god, not of a man!" Immediately, because Herod did not give praise to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he died. But the word of God continued to spread and flourish. Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, taking John Mark with them.

summary.bigIdea: While the church prays, God rescues Peter from prison, and proud Herod falls, but God's word keeps spreading.
points: James is killed and Peter imprisoned by King Herod.
The church prays, and an angel leads Peter out of prison.
Herod takes glory for himself and dies; the word of God spreads.
summary.reflection: The church prayed, yet was astonished when Peter turned up! Do you ever pray without expecting God to act?
